← How it’s built

The map

Everything the project knows and does, hung on one register of concepts. Four spines: the simulated world, the supplier’s value chain, the running of the company, and how the whole thing is built. The register is small and kept by hand; every link and every gap below is generated from it at publish, from what the code and documents already say.

This is the pilot: two slices are mapped, supplier ‘Collect’ and How it’s built ‘Testing and controls’. A step in a dashed box is not on the register yet. Tap a concept to open it; its links jump across spines.

Beliefs and decisions

The data the supplier decides on: each belief is built only from what crosses the wall, feeds named decisions, and is graded against the simulation's hidden truth.

Forward cash forecast per customer

Built from bills, payments and returns, payment method, the account's record

The belief, in code company.finance.cash_forecast_provision called

Decides provision, payment plans, early warnings

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's hidden payments yet

Consumption forecast per property

Built from reads, registered consumption, weather

The belief, in code company.billing.consumption_forecast not in the tree

Decides direct debit amount, unbilled estimate, purchasing, CLV

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's true consumption yet

Can't pay versus won't pay

Built from payment history, contact record, declared circumstances

The belief, in code company.crm.affordability_inference called

Decides payment plan level, support referral, collections tone

Graded against the truth Gap: no grade against the world's hidden finances yet

Measures, one definition each

A measure carries what it counts, over whom, and the one function that computes it. The ranges a knowledge page states about the drawn world are measures too, and come from tools/world_claims.py.

  • Direct debit failure rate: counts collections returned unpaid, over collections presented in the period. Computed by Gap: no function is named as its one definition yet.
  • direct_debit_share_of_accounts, stated on gb_payment_method_migration_rates: published range 66.5% to 75.5%, checked against the drawn world by tools.world_claims._direct_debit_share_of_accounts. DESNZ Quarterly Energy Prices, Dec 2025 commentary, p.9: standard electricity DD 69% (Sept 2020) to 72% (Sept 2025), gas to 73%.

Minimum capital requirement capital.mcr

A domestic supplier holds at least zero, and aims for £115, of adjusted net assets per dual-fuel customer, from 31 March 2025.

Taken from: SLC 4B; Ofgem financial resilience decision (26 Jul 2023)

Also called: capital target, capital floor, adjusted net assets, mcr

What the map flags

  • World rule: capital is the company's own; the world holds no rule for it
  • Crosses the wall: nothing crosses: the company reads its own balance sheet

Also called: cash coverage trigger, customer credit balances, ringfencing

What the map flags

Connect and notify network.connect_and_notify

Cut-out rating and supply phase network.cut_out_rating

The amp rating of the DNO's main fuse at the home (typically 60-100 A) and whether the supply is single- or three-phase; together they bound what can be added before an application.

Also called: main fuse rating, cut-out fuse, fuse upgrade, three-phase supply

What the map flags

  • World rule: no home carries a cut-out rating or phase; a 22 kW charger is drawn regardless
  • Crosses the wall: not visible to a supplier
  • Supplier feature: none

No link from here.

Third-party flexibility capture optimise.third_party_flex

An independent party trades or balances a supplier's customer's demand turn-down or turn-up, and the supplier is compensated for the resulting deviation at a reference price funded by all suppliers by market share.

Taken from: BSC P415 (live 7 Nov 2024); Supplier Compensation Reference Price Methodology v2.0; P444; P510 and P511

Also called: virtual trading party, virtual lead party, vtp, deviation volume, supplier compensation

What the map flags

  • World rule: no rival aggregator agent exists; no MSID is ever claimed by another party
  • Crosses the wall: no compensation or deviation volume crosses
  • Supplier feature: nothing books compensation or the mutualisation levy

How it connects, across all four spines

No link from here.

Local network flexibility optimise.dno_flexibility

A distribution network buys demand turn-down or turn-up in named zones through standard products, paying availability per MW per hour and utilisation per MWh, settled per minute with a performance multiplier.

Taken from: ENA Open Networks standard products; Elexon Flexibility Market Rules FMR-VSM (30 Jan 2026) and FMR-SBM; DNO SLC31E reports

Also called: dno flexibility, dso flexibility, flexibility zone, peak reduction, scheduled utilisation

What the map flags
